title: The four-day week
summary_es: Entrevista de pódcast al director de una pequeña empresa de software que pasó a toda su plantilla a la semana de cuatro días.
prediction_prompt: A company moves everyone to a four-day week with the same pay. What problems and benefits would you expect?

segments.speaker: hannah
segments.text: Welcome back to Work in Progress. Today we're talking about the four-day week.

segments.speaker: hannah
segments.text: My guest is Daniel Reyes, who runs a small software company in Denver.

segments.speaker: hannah
segments.text: Daniel, you moved your whole team to four days last year. What made you do it?

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: Honestly, we were losing people. Three of our best developers had left within six months.

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: They weren't going to competitors for more money. They were simply exhausted.

segments.speaker: hannah
segments.text: So it wasn't really about productivity at first?

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: Not at all. I was just trying to stop people from walking out the door.

segments.speaker: hannah
segments.text: And how did you actually organise it? Did everybody take Friday off?

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: That was the original plan, but our clients still needed support on Fridays.

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: So half the team takes Monday off and the other half takes Friday.

segments.speaker: hannah
segments.text: Did you cut salaries?

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: No. Same pay, fewer hours. If we'd cut pay, nobody would have trusted the experiment.

segments.speaker: hannah
segments.text: I imagine some people were sceptical.

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: My business partner certainly was. She thought we'd get eighty percent of the work done.

segments.speaker: hannah
segments.text: And did you?

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: Surprisingly, no. Output stayed almost exactly the same, and in some months it went up.

segments.speaker: hannah
segments.text: How do you explain that?

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: Mostly meetings. We used to have about twelve hours of meetings a week per person.

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: We cut that to four, and suddenly people had time to do their real work.

segments.speaker: hannah
segments.text: Were there any downsides?

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: Sure. The four days are intense, and not everybody likes that.

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: One colleague told me she missed the slower afternoons, when you could chat and have ideas.

segments.speaker: hannah
segments.text: That's something you rarely hear in discussions about this.

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: Exactly. It's a real cost, and we haven't solved it yet.

segments.speaker: hannah
segments.text: Interesting. Would you ever go back to five days?

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: I doubt it. Nobody has resigned since we changed, and applications have tripled.

segments.speaker: daniel
segments.text: But I wouldn't tell every company to copy us. It depends on what you do.

segments.speaker: hannah
segments.text: Daniel Reyes, thank you very much for joining us.

connected_speech.explanation_es: En inglés americano las dos *t* entre vocales suenan como una *r* suave, y las tres palabras se enlazan: «nárarol».
*have* se reduce a /əv/ y se pega a *would*: suena «wúdav». Es fácil oír *would of*.
*we'd* = *we would*. La *d* casi desaparece delante de la *g*.
*had* y *to* son débiles (/həd/, /tə/): el acento cae en *time* y *do*.

tasks.prompt: What is the interview mainly about?

options.text: Why software developers now earn less than they used to
How to run meetings online more efficiently
A firm's experience of working fewer days
The best way to find new clients

tasks.rationale_es: Hannah lo anuncia al empezar: hablan de la semana de cuatro días y de lo que le pasó a la empresa de Daniel al adoptarla.

tasks.prompt: How does Daniel feel about the change overall?

options.text: Positive, but aware of its limits
Disappointed that the team produced less
Angry with his business partner
Sure that every company should follow his example

tasks.rationale_es: Está contento con los resultados, pero reconoce un coste real que no han resuelto y dice que no se lo recomendaría a todas las empresas.

tasks.prompt: Why did Daniel first consider a four-day week?

options.text: To attract more clients to the company
To keep his staff from leaving
To save money on salaries
To copy what a competitor was doing

tasks.rationale_es: Estaban perdiendo gente (*we were losing people*) y él solo quería que dejaran de marcharse.

tasks.prompt: The developers who left went to work for competitors.
tasks.rationale_es: *They weren't going to competitors*: no se iban a la competencia, sino que estaban agotados.

tasks.prompt: How is the week organised now?

options.text: Everyone in the company has the same day off
The office is closed to clients one day a week
People choose a different day each week
The staff are split between two different days off

tasks.rationale_es: La mitad libra el lunes y la otra mitad el viernes, porque los clientes seguían necesitando asistencia los viernes.

options.text: They were reduced by twenty percent
They did not change
They went up a little
They now depend on results

tasks.rationale_es: *Same pay, fewer hours*: el mismo sueldo por menos horas.

tasks.prompt: Why did Daniel decide not to cut pay?

options.text: He feared staff would not believe in the trial
The law in his state did not allow him to do it
His partner refused
Clients would have complained

tasks.rationale_es: *If we'd cut pay, nobody would have trusted the experiment*: sin el sueldo íntegro, nadie se habría fiado de la prueba.

tasks.prompt: Daniel's business partner expected the amount of work to fall.
tasks.rationale_es: Ella pensaba que solo sacarían el ochenta por ciento del trabajo, es decir, que bajaría.

options.text: Clients are less satisfied than before

The working days feel more intense
Meetings have become much longer

tasks.rationale_es: *The four days are intense, and not everybody likes that*. Lo de encontrar personal es al revés: las solicitudes se han triplicado.

tasks.prompt: Daniel is planning to open a second office.
tasks.rationale_es: Habla de que nadie ha dimitido y de que hay más solicitudes, pero no menciona ninguna oficina nueva.

tasks.prompt: What does Daniel suggest at the end of the interview?

options.text: He is thinking of returning to a five-day week
Small firms cannot afford this kind of change
All companies should adopt the model soon
The model may not suit every business

tasks.rationale_es: *I wouldn't tell every company to copy us. It depends on what you do*: no vale para todas.

tasks.reference: Not at all. I was just trying to stop people from walking out the door.
